newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas slips on warmer weather and ample supply.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas slips on warmer weather and ample supply.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market started to slip on Wednesday following several days of higher prices, traders and brokers said.

Trade was done in three distinct periods, they said. A large volume of day ahead gas or gas for two days forward was done; there was then a spate of trades in the third quarter this year at significantly lower prices; and there was also a number of deals in winter 1997/98. Prices were off by around 0.10 pence a therm in all periods, traders said, although Q3 97 slipped further.
"Summer 97 came down with the warmer weather and the realisation that there's a lot of gas out there," said a dealer.

Another pointed to a switch of positions as buyers became sellers, especially in the winter, as a reason for the fall. "There's just a lack of bids supporting it and a lot of sellers out there," he said. "People have turned around."

And several players who are frequently active on the market were not participating on Wednesday because of paperwork generated by the last day of the month. One seller at St Fergus, for example, reported posting prices in the morning slightly above Tuesday's levels "in the hope of dragging it up, but there were no takers."

Even though he knew the price was slipping, he did not adjust levels because of attention to administrative matters, and consequently did not conclude any trade apart from some short term deals. Some other players reported effectively keeping off the market for similar reasons.

Warmer weather is driving demand down significantly. Thursday's demand is forecast by Transco at 171 mcm, or 40 percent of peak day demand. This compares with a Wednesday demand figure of 183 mcm or 43 percent, and with 205 mcm (48 percent) on Tuesday. The temperature on Thursday is forecast at 14.8 Celsius against a seasonal normal 11.3 Celsius.

The IPE futures market traded 155 lots, all but 5 of them in June and July. A single player was involved in every one of the June and July trades, which were done at slightly higher prices than on Tuesday.
